evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line that produced the two -8% prints in the baseline. 2026-03-24: FY2025 PAC of EUR59.7m matched only Kepler Cheuvreux's PESSIMISTIC EUR60m case against an optimistic EUR66m, net income EUR25.1m against Kepler's EUR27.8m and EPS EUR0.42 against EUR0.47 — the stock fell 8.19% on the day despite a simultaneously disclosed +40% activity pace. 2024-03-26 fell 8.34% on the same line. What is unpriced is the conversion and the fact that nothing has moved to reflect it. If the market had absorbed it, the two covering analysts would not still be carrying price targets 'last updated on Mar 24, 2026' (stockanalysis/S&P Global), the FY2026 revenue estimate would not still read EUR69.75m — which requires June-December 2026 to run at EUR3.92m/month, 21% BELOW the 2025 average and 54% below the disclosed Jan-May 2026 rate — and the stock would not be at EUR5.25 against EUR5.33 on the morning of the release, nearer its EUR4.87 52-week low than its EUR6.19 high, with a 20-day run-up of +1.74%. A French analyst wrote the same observation into a headline on 2026-09-03: 'nette acceleration de l'activite, mais le titre reste sans reaction'. Coverage is 2 analysts on $276k/day of turnover, the band where nobody is positioned for a confirmed fact. This size is already NET of the two things that break the conversion and broke the March print: approximately 45% of value created is redistributed to staff as variable compensation, and Momentum 2028 adds about EUR3m of incremental investment across full-year 2026 — ABC Bourse makes exactly this objection ('Cette phase de developpement pourrait temporairement limiter la conversion de la hausse d'activite en resultat net'). I have netted it here rather than carrying it as a second, contradictory finding.

evidence.text: The obvious bear read of the H2-to-date pace comment — index VIX at its 2026 low, therefore a repeat of the H2 2025 collapse that got the last September print sold — is probably keyed to the wrong market parameter: the company states the Jan-May surge happened in conditions 'broadly comparable' to the prior year, making it capability rather than weather, and H2 2026 has carried record single-stock dispersion with S&P 500 pairwise correlation in the bottom 1% since 2005.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the decisive line on this name in September. On 2025-09-23 the reported half was outstanding — net income doubled, ROE 20.3%, two EUR0.10 interims declared — and the stock fell 1.51%, because the release flagged that volatility had returned to historically low levels since June and H2 activity was down on H1. Kepler's later summary of that year confirms the mechanism: 'l'annee a ete marquee par un premier semestre tres solide, suivi de conditions de marche moins favorables au second semestre'. Conversely on 2026-03-24 a +40% pace statement was NOT enough to save a print whose P&L missed. So a constructive pace comment is necessary but not sufficient, and a weak one is close to sufficient for a negative day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The visible, quotable, terminal-level statistic on volatility is the VIX, and it is at its 2026 low — 14.2 on 2026-08-14 and 14.81 at the close on 2026-09-18, down from 21.51 in early June. Anyone previewing this print off the wire copy reaches for that number and reproduces the September-2025 trade. What the VIX does not describe is the environment a relative-value arbitrageur is actually paid in: on 2026-07-09 the Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index closed at 49.98 against a VIX of 15.84, an all-time record 34.14-point gap and the 98th percentile for VIXEQ, and as of 2026-08-14 the average 60-day pairwise correlation among S&P 500 constituents sat in the bottom 1% of observations since 2005. Low index vol produced by low correlation and high single-stock vol is the opposite regime, for this business, from the genuinely quiet summer of 2025. If the market had made this distinction the stock would not be flat-to-down through a quarter in which its own disclosed activity pace accelerated from +40% (20 March) to +70% (end May). I am sizing this at less than half of finding 1 because LESSONS.md is explicit that macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and no [THE COMPANY] document names dispersion; the company statement I quote covers January-May, not July-September.

evidence.text: The 22 September release is the scheduled venue for the first half-yearly distribution decision under the new semi-annual policy, where an already-announced EUR0.20 December interim has to be reconciled with an H1 EPS near EUR0.36-0.40 and a stated 66% payout ratio — against a consensus 2026 DPS of only EUR0.35 on a stock already yielding 6.5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution is the single most reliably price-moving line on this name, and it has cut both ways. The 2025-09-23 half-year release declared two EUR0.10 interims and the stock still fell 1.51%. The 2026-03-24 release cut the total 2025 distribution shape to EUR0.34 with an 81% payout and the stock fell 8.19%. In a EUR314m name held largely for a 6.3-6.5% yield, a distribution that merely meets what was already announced is worth nothing and one that lags is worth several points; the asymmetry here is that a raise has not been contemplated by the unrevised estimates.
evidence.why_not_priced: The EUR0.20 is public, so a bare confirmation is neutral and that is why this is the smallest of the three sizes. What is not in the estimates is the arithmetic that a half earning EUR0.36-0.40 per share makes EUR0.20 a ~52% half-year payout against a stated 66% policy, leaving visible headroom at the very moment the board first exercises the new semi-annual mechanism. If the market were carrying that, the 2026 DPS line in consensus would not still read EUR0.35 — barely above the EUR0.34 paid for 2025 — and the yield would not still be 6.48% on a name whose run-rate earnings are ~39% higher than the year that produced it. The offsetting risk, which is why the low end of my band is negative: the 2025 annual release also signalled an intention to strengthen equity via a dividend-reinvestment option from end-2026, and an income-oriented French retail base can read a scrip option as cash retention rather than as capital-return growth.
evidence.independence: The semi-annual switch and the EUR0.20 figure are independently reported by a second French outlet: [url removed] (2026-03-24). The policy floor and payout ratio are in the issuer's own English release, [url removed] . This finding rests on a different document from findings 1 and 2.

evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic forces a fork the five models on this name cannot both have taken, and consensus reconciles to the naive branch. R&D is roughly four-fifths of Ambarella's opex, so a $9.0m credit is a ~20% cut to the R&D line; for reported non-GAAP opex still to land inside $56-59m the underlying run-rate would have to have jumped ~16% sequentially with zero explanation given. Consensus of a ($0.30) GAAP loss on 5 estimates bridges almost exactly off the $56-59m guide midpoint at face value, which is what you get when analysts take the guide and never open the footnote. So either the credit sits on top of the guide as an unguided ~$0.21/share benefit, or it is silently inside it and Q3 opex must step back up ~$9m - and management has said nothing that lets the market tell which. Had this been priced, at least one of the press release, the prepared remarks or the Q&A would have carried the words 'one-time' or 'credit', and none does.

The company has never disclosed the composition or counterparties of the line; its stated definition includes 'marketing services to insurance companies, insurance brokers, and agency companies', i.e. a gross-up of resold traffic, which is exactly why S&M rose 213.8% for 5.3% more operating profit.

evidence.why_not_priced: No wire service, screener or estimate aggregator week-adjusts a 53-week fiscal year; the Q1 FY26 release buried it in the clause 'which included an extra week' and the $50.7m base is carried forward raw everywhere. If this were priced, the sell-side revenue estimate would sit near $49-50m (13/14ths of a flat comp) rather than $53.2m, and the pre-print commentary would frame the quarter as a like-for-like acceleration instead of a 5% YoY step-up. It sets up a release in which the YoY revenue and gross-margin comparisons understate the underlying improvement, which management will point out on the 10 Sept call.
evidence.independence: The fiscal calendar is corroborated independently by the 10-K, whose fiscal year ends 2026-05-03 against the prior 2025-04-27 - 371 days, i.e. 53 weeks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm (filed 2026-07-17)

evidence.text: Culp issued its Q1 FY27 guidance on 2026-07-01 for a quarter that ended 2026-08-02 - i.e. with roughly 9 of 13 weeks already elapsed and the $7.0m tariff refund cash already in hand - so 'breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA without the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds' and 'net debt of approximately $5.0 million by first quarter-end' are near-observed facts, not forecasts.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline's expected move is a 6.02% median drawn from seven prints of which six went down - all of them delivered mid-restructuring with no forward guidance and genuinely uncertain outcomes. This print is the opposite: the guide was set two-thirds of the way through the quarter with the one-time cash already received. If the market had processed that the outcome distribution is narrow, the run-up would not be a directionless -0.58% over 20 days and the 5-day drift would not be a 17,000-share-a-day random walk; a stock about to resolve a genuinely uncertain 6% event trades differently into it. The residual is that Culp's downside tail here is much thinner than its own reaction history implies.
evidence.independence: Shares a source document with finding 3 below (the 2026-07-01 EX-99.1) - flagging the cluster. Separately corroborated by the FY26 10-K, which reports only $4.426m of full-year D&A, meaning the EBITDA-to-EPS bridge is small and the guide translates almost directly into the reported number: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723603/000119312526307064/culp-20260503.htm

evidence.why_not_priced: The default failure mode when a microcap books a one-time gain of this size is that the company headlines an ex-item loss and the tape prints a catastrophic-looking miss against a GAAP-basis estimate.
